W7223937057.abstract: Clinical expertise is inherently distributed: it resides not in any single dataset or institution but in the accumulated reasoning experiences of thousands of clinicians navigating diverse patient populations, resource constraints, and evolving treatment protocols. Yet current approaches to scaling medical AI, from centralized large language models to federated learning, remain anchored to a data-centric paradigm that treats knowledge as static parameters to be aggregated. In this Perspective, we argue for a fundamental shift from data aggregation to experience aggregation. We propose Decentralized Agentic Systems (DAS), a framework in which distributed AI agents operating across healthcare institutions synthesize collective clinical intelligence by sharing abstracted reasoning trajectories rather than raw data or model parameters. Unlike federated learning, which averages numerical gradients across homogeneous model architectures, DAS exchanges structured records of clinical reasoning, specifically the sequence of observations, hypotheses, tool invocations, and outcome feedback that constitute diagnostic experience. We examine the architectural principles, deployment considerations, governance requirements, and critical open challenges of this framework, laying the groundwork for a collaborative medical AI ecosystem where distributed expertise autonomously adapts to the complexities of longitudinal patient care.

W7224082740.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a prevalent yet incompletely understood functional gastrointestinal disorder whose estimated prevalence depends heavily on the diagnostic criteria applied, falling from approximately 9% under Rome III to approximately 4% under Rome IV. Characterized by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits, it substantially impairs quality of life and imposes a considerable economic burden. Its pathophysiology is complex and multifactorial, involving visceral hypersensitivity, altered gastrointestinal motility, immune activation, gut-brain axis dysregulation, and intestinal dysbiosis. This narrative review examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to refine the diagnosis, subclassification, and management of IBS and related functional gastrointestinal disorders. We discuss the principal AI methodologies - machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing - and how they enable the integration of diverse data sources, including patient-reported outcomes, microbiome profiles, and multi-omics data. Early studies suggest AI can support the differentiation of IBS from organic disease, the identification of biologically distinct microbiota subgroups, and the prediction of response to the low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols diet. These findings, however, derive largely from small, single-center cohorts with heterogeneous methods and without external validation; a 2025 systematic review identified only six eligible studies comprising 1366 participants and found the evidence too heterogeneous to permit meta-analysis. We further identify domains in which AI is frequently invoked but not yet evidenced in IBS, including machine-learning analysis of longitudinal patient-collected symptom data and of psychological comorbidity. Substantial challenges remain around data standardization, external and temporal validation, model interpretability, and ethical and regulatory considerations. Progress will depend less on the development of further models than on standardized data collection, multi-center validation, and reporting against AI-specific standards such as transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis + AI.

W7224285487.abstract: Document understanding requires answering questions over long, multi-page documents that interleave text, figures, and tables.Recent methods adopt the Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation (DocRAG) paradigm, which indexes each document and feeds the top-K most relevant pages to a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) per query.Because each page can be represented as extracted text or a rendered image, DocRAG systems expose two key knobs: an indexing modality choice when the documents are ingested and a context modality at query time.Existing systems either fix both knobs to the visual modality or use both modalities throughout, often incurring higher indexing and query costs than needed for a given document or query.We propose AdaptiveDocRAG, which adapts both knobs as well as the size of the visual context to optimize the trade-off between accuracy, query response time, and indexing time.AdaptiveDocRAG achieves this through three lightweight modules.First, documentadaptive indexing modality selection uses a text-density heuristic to route text-dominant documents to cheaper textual indexing.Second, query-adaptive context modality selection uses a learned per-query router to select textual or visual context.Third, query-aware visual context compression reuses the retriever's per-patch query-page similarity to crop relevant sub-page regions and fuse them with topranked text chunks.On MMLongBench-Doc and NQ-Text with Qwen3-VL-8B, Adaptive-DocRAG matches or improves upon the accuracy of visual-only DocRAG (up to +1.1 points) while using ∼50% of the MLLM tokens, resulting in 1.30-1.79×end-to-end speedup and 1.34× faster indexing.

W7224632907.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAC) remains the most lethal malignancies, with a 5-year survival rate of only around 12%. The dismal prognosis is largely attributable to late diagnosis, as early PAC is frequently asymptomatic and radiologically inconspicuous. Contemporary international guidelines recommend surveillance for well-defined high-risk groups, particularly carriers of pathogenic germline mutations such as BRCA2, STK11, and CDKN2A, as well as familial pancreatic cancer kindreds. In these settings, endoscopic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging are the recommended surveillance modalities. Recent advances in biomarker discovery, including circulating tumor DNA, methylation signatures of cell-free DNA, and extracellular vesicles, have demonstrated encouraging results, particularly when combined with CA19-9. Paraneoplastic phenomena such as pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes and cancer-induced cachexia provide additional opportunities for earlier clinical recognition. Parallel progress has been achieved in artificial intelligence-driven radiomics analysis and deep learning algorithms, which can increase the sensitivity of cross-sectional imaging for small or otherwise occult lesions. The integration of clinical risk stratification, molecular biomarkers, and AI-enhanced imaging represents a promising framework to shift diagnosis toward surgically resectable stages. This review synthesizes the current evidence, highlights recent advances, and discusses practical considerations for physicians to facilitate earlier detection of PAC.

W7224764794.abstract: The rapid development of cloud technology, big data, and artificial intelligence has changed the way data pipelines are managed in today’s world. Conventional data pipeline management systems depend on rule-based automation and manual intervention making them less effective in managing dynamic workloads, detecting anomalies, recovering from faults, and optimizing resources. The recent advances in Agentic Artificial Intelligence, LLMs, reinforcement learning, and multi-agent systems have given rise to the autonomous systems that can perform monitoring, diagnosis, recovery, and optimization on their own. This review studies the state-of-the-art AI information pipeline management processes, intelligent work flow orchestration, autonomous decision making, and self-healing systems. The paper reviews the existing methodologies, including ETL automation, metadata-based data ingestion, optimization through reinforcement learning, and agent-based orchestration systems, and presents their advantages, limitations, and potential fields of application. Moreover, the review identifies main research problems faced by researchers and developers including explainability, interoperability, scalability, security, and adaptation in heterogeneous cloud environments.

W7224773515.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and represents one of the greatest challenges facing contemporary medicine because of its high prevalence, irreversible progression, and profound impact on patients, their families, and healthcare systems. The present study aimed to analyze recent scientific advances in the diagnosis and therapeutic strategies for Alzheimer's disease through an integrative review of specialized literature. To achieve this objective, a qualitative analysis of scientific publications was conducted. The findings reveal a significant transformation in the diagnostic paradigm, shifting from an approach based primarily on clinical assessment to one supported by biological biomarkers, advanced neuroimaging techniques, and precision medicine strategies capable of identifying neuropathological changes during the preclinical stages of the disease. Likewise, the literature demonstrates a substantial shift in treatment approaches, moving from symptomatic management toward interventions designed to modify disease progression. Important advances were also identified in the fields of artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, precision pharmacology, and the development of innovative drug discovery platforms. Although significant challenges remain regarding biological heterogeneity, clinical efficacy, safety, accessibility, and the implementation of these innovations, the available scientific evidence indicates that the future management of Alzheimer's disease will be based on early diagnosis, molecular patient stratification, and the development of personalized therapeutic strategies capable of delaying neurodegeneration and improving clinical outcomes.

W7225142504.abstract: Software development and applications have changed significantly with the widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs). Conversational chatbots now enable intuitive interaction through natural language. This industrial experience report presents the development of a healthcare platform centered on an AI-powered chatbot, named Hemachat, built on an LLM-based multi-agent system. This solution aims to support both healthcare professionals and patients with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) by assisting with medical follow-up, tracking laboratory examinations and consultation schedules, answering general questions about the disease, and supporting patient triage. Furthermore, it generates treatment plans that can assist physicians in the clinical decision-making process. This report focuses on the development steps, the software architecture, and the major software engineering decisions that shaped the system. It further discusses key challenges, including privacy and security, testing AI-powered conversational systems, and ensuring reliable and clinically safe behaviour in a safety-critical healthcare environment. While reporting the development experience and identifying open challenges, we aim to provide practical insights to support developers of multiagent LLM-based healthcare applications.

W7225161827.abstract: The rapid deployment of autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents capable of invoking external tools, managing persistent memory, and orchestrating multi-agent workflows has outpaced the development of principled security architectures. Existing approaches rely predominantly on prompt-level heuristics or model alignment, which are demonstrably insufficient against adversarial inputs such as prompt injection, indirect tool-call manipulation, and privilege escalation across agent chains. This paper proposes a formal reference monitor framework—the Agent Reference Monitor (ARM)—that treats the LLM as an untrusted, confined process and enforces policy at the tool-call boundary using classical security concepts: Mandatory Access Control (MAC), Information Flow Control (IFC), and capability-based confinement. We present the ARM architecture,a threat taxonomy specific to LLM agents, and a comparative analysis with FIDES, CaMeL, ClawGuard, and NeuroTaint, alongside a prototype implementation and IEEE educational workshop series.

W7225175605.abstract: We present \textbf{UniCaMo}, an unified framework for joint control of camera and object motion in image-and-text-to-video diffusion models. Given a reference image, text prompt, sparse 3D object trajectories, and a 3D camera trajectory, UniCaMo constructs motion-consistent input noise that directly encodes the desired motion. Our 3D-grounded noise construction combines reference-derived noise propagation with a spherical Gaussian noise representation for newly revealed regions, providing a simple and effective motion prior without requiring reconstruction of unseen scene geometry. UniCaMo requires no architectural modifications or dedicated control modules and can be adapted using lightweight LoRA fine-tuning with low training data volume. Experiments on standard controllable video generation benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art motion controllability and high visual quality with minimal inference overhead.

W7225177501.abstract: Extracting knowledge from large databases of experimental materials data requires repeated analyses and reusable records of their choices and results. We developed Multi-Agentic AI (MAA), a multi-agent system in which AI agents with distinct roles analyze experimental thermoelectric data under predefined instructions and quality checks, saving analysis records traceable to their sources. In four experiments varying theme and cycle counts, we measured what accumulated in these records. In the largest experiment (100 analyses across 10 themes and 10 cycles), concept co-occurrences were concentrated within themes, vocabulary was shared across themes and some relation descriptions were first detected in later cycles. A specialized AI that searches this experiment's knowledge bases and reads their analysis records answered materials questions with cited sources. Retrospective checks, including tracing an answer generated with a preliminary corpus back to the source data, exposed errors: traceability makes errors findable but not absent.

W7225253582.abstract: Objectives: This study proposes an intelligent Cognitive Artificial Intelligence (CAI) framework for expanding knowledge through the integration of machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), reinforcement learning, and cognitive computing techniques. The research aims to develop an intelligent cognitive agent capable of understanding user queries, generating meaningful insights from historical data, supporting personalized learning, and improving educational decision-making through continuous knowledge acquisition and adaptive learning. Theoretical Framework: The study is grounded in the principles of cognitive computing, artificial intelligence, machine learning, natural language processing, agent-based computing, knowledge-based systems, and reinforcement learning. It integrates these complementary technologies into a unified cognitive architecture that supports knowledge discovery, intelligent question answering, answer recommendation, confidence evaluation, and continuous learning from user feedback. Methodology: A design and implementation research approach was adopted to develop the proposed Cognitive Artificial Intelligence framework. A cognitive question-answering agent (CogQA Edu) was designed using Natural Language Processing, Knowledge Base, Agent-Based Computing, Confidence Value System, Answer Recommendation System, and Cognitive Computing modules. The Electrical Motor domain was selected as a case study for prototype implementation. System performance was experimentally evaluated by subject-matter experts using multiple evaluation metrics, including First Hit Success (FHS), First Answer Right Rate (FARR), First Answer Wrong Rate (FARWR), Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Total Response Rate (TRR), Precision, and Recall. Findings: The experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed cognitive agent effectively understands natural language queries, retrieves contextually relevant knowledge, and provides accurate answer recommendations supported by confidence scores. The integration of machine learning, NLP, and cognitive computing significantly improves knowledge extraction, intelligent reasoning, personalized educational support, and decision-making compared with conventional educational information retrieval systems. The feedback-driven learning mechanism further enhances system adaptability and prediction accuracy over time. Research Implications: The proposed framework provides practical guidance for educational institutions, intelligent tutoring systems, and AI developers by demonstrating how cognitive computing architectures can improve personalized learning, automated knowledge management, intelligent question answering, and educational decision support. The study also establishes a foundation for future research on autonomous cognitive agents and Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Value: This study contributes to the field of Cognitive Artificial Intelligence by proposing and implementing an integrated cognitive agent that combines machine learning, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, agent-based computing, and cognitive computing within a unified architecture. The proposed framework advances intelligent educational systems by enabling adaptive knowledge expansion, context-aware reasoning, and continuous learning, providing a practical step toward next-generation autonomous cognitive agents.

W7225413038.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are being integrated into multi-agent systems (MAS), which is exponentially growing and presenting not just capabilities for collaborative problem solving and autonomous decision making but also adaptive coordination. By providing natural language understanding, dynamic role assignment, and contextualised reasoning capabilities, LLM-based agents provide more adaptable and human-like ways for traditional MAS agents to interact with each other. The advantages of LLM-based agents can be seen in many applications where agents must communicate, cooperate and compete effectively; examples include automated negotiation, swarm robotics and decentralized artificial intelligence (AI). Nevertheless, LLM-MAS face significant challenges, including maintaining coherence across multiple agents during conversations, reducing biases in LLM outputs and hallucination events, and optimising computational efficiency when deploying LLMs on a large scale. Some recent work has explored creating hybrid architectures that combine LLMs and symbolic reasoning, reinforcement learning, and game theory-based approaches to increase robustness and scalability of LLM-MAS. Ethical considerations like accountability and alignment in LLM-MAS that are decentralised also need to be addressed. The role of LLMs in MAS is expected to continue to expand as LLMs develop, leading to greater sophistication of autonomous systems in smart cities, science discovery, and human-AI collaboration. Future research directions may focus on creating specialised agents to better resolve conflicts, developing processes for secure and explainable multi-agent collaboration and integrating new tools into MAS (e.g. LLMs, game theory) to improve operational performance of automated decision makers. Next-generation intelligent systems that are more flexible, scalable, and capable of handling challenging real-world tasks might be made possible by the rising synergy between LLMs and MAS.

W7225422280.abstract: The title of a playlist often reflects an intended mood or theme, allowing creators to easily locate their content and enabling other users to discover music that matches specific situations and needs. This work presents a novel approach to playlist generation using language models to leverage the thematic coherence between a playlist title and its tracks. Our method consists of creating semantic clusters from text embeddings, followed by fine-tuning a transformer model on these thematic clusters. Playlists are then generated considering the cosine similarity scores between known and unknown titles and applying a ranking mechanism, for which we compare a voting system and an LLM-based ranker. Performance evaluation, combining quantitative and qualitative metrics, demonstrates that using the playlist title as a seed provides useful recommendations, even in a zero-shot scenario.

W7225449978.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state lithium metal batteries suffer from poor interfacial stability and dendrite growth, primarily limited by the ion transport kinetics and mechanical properties of composite solid electrolytes (CSE). Inspired by the hierarchical grape cluster, we design a biomimetic electrolyte via electrospinning PAN fiber “pedicel” integrated with mesoporous SiO 2 ‐SO 3 Li “grape berry” fillers, followed by in‐situ polymerization. This structure establishes long‐range Li + conduction channels and a robust physical barrier, delivering a high Li + transference number of 0.65, ionic conductivity of 1.44 × 10 −3 S cm −1 at 25°C, and a modulus of 520 MPa. Benefiting from these advantages, the assembled LFP|Li and NCM811|Li cells achieve 88.8% capacity retention after 1000 cycles and 94.3% after 300 cycles, respectively. Moreover, a high‐loading pouch cell realizes an energy density of 414.9 Wh kg −1 /797.8 Wh L −1 and withstands harsh abuse tests. Mechanistically, DFT and phase‐field simulations reveal the dual Li + pathways and TFSI − immobilization enabled by the ‐SO 3 Li groups. Notably, a physics‐informed neural network (PINN) framework decouples interface activation‐aging kinetics and predicts long‐term impedance evolution. This work provides a biomimetic paradigm and data‐driven methods for the design and interface analysis of high‐performance CSE.
